{{Quote|Don't mess with these guys. It's not worth it.|[[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]], discussing the Mandalorian Patrol|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
The '''Mandalorian Patrol''' was an organization of [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Fleet/Legends|space forces]] responsible for protecting the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|outbreak]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. A unit of the larger [[Mandalorian Guard/Legends|Mandalorian Guard]], the Patrol acted as a [[Planetary Security Forces|Planetary Security Force]], intercepting [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and other suspicious [[Starship/Legends|craft]]. Over [[Time/Legends|time]], the members of the Mandalorian Patrol developed a more aggressive reputation than their contemporaries among the ranks of the Mandalorian Guard, and were known to make use of [[Death/Legends|deadly]] force if the situation required it. The Patrol possessed few [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]], and though they employed a number of [[Heavy cruiser/Legends|heavy cruisers]] in the course of their operations, Patrolmen more commonly relied on smaller, faster [[Patrol ship/Legends|patrol craft]], supported by [[Corvette/Legends|corvettes]] and [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]].<ref name="TBHC" />

During the intersocietal struggle between the competing ideologies of the traditional [[True Mandalorians]], the pacifistic [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]], and the radical [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]],<ref name="TEGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> the Mandalorian Patrol was known to contain several members who sympathized with the Death Watch's cause. In his training manifesto entitled ''[[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad]]'', Death Watch [[Secret Mandalore|leader]] [[Tor Vizsla]] instructed his [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] to avoid confrontation with the Patrol. Death Watch had become adept at learning the routes and maneuvers of the Mandalorian Patrol, allowing the two organizations to keep out of each other's way, and Patrolmen with Death Watch sympathies were seen as promising candidates for potential recruitment.<ref name="TBHC" />

Several [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] later, the [[Imperial Military/Legends|forces]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] occupied Mandalore and [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] its people. After a lengthy struggle, [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] [[Fenn Shysa]] and the [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]] finally succeeded in driving the Imperial forces from their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. From that point on, the Mandalorian Protectors' fleet of [[Pursuer-class enforcement ship|''Pursuer''-class ships]]<ref name="GaW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> assumed many of the duties previously performed by the Mandalorian Patrol.<ref name="TBHC" /> The Protectors patrolled Mandalorian space, attacking and boarding any hostile vessels that ventured into their territory, before delivering the captive starship to [[Keldabe spaceport|Mandalore's spaceport]]<ref name="GaW" /> in the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Mandalorian Patrol was first introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe in ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', a reference book co-[[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Jason Fry]], [[Daniel Wallace]], and [[Ryder Windham]], and released on [[October 15]], [[2013]].<ref name="TBHC" />
